factor_ratings.evidence: Scope limited to a single sub-block (CDC synchronizer and register-map RTL) within one larger PHY controller block; impact contained within the immediate team.
Wrote and verified RTL 'under supervision' as a new-grad -- work assigned and reviewed in detail.
CDC synchronizer and register-map design have known solution paths/patterns, though require some proficiency to implement correctly.
Described as a new-grad RTL designer developing proficiency in RTL design under supervision; no evidence of independent mastery yet.
Owned a sub-block, not a full block or module end to end -- below the L3 anchor of 'owns a block or module end to end'; carried it through only 1 tapeout under supervision.
No evidence of influence beyond immediate team; communicates within the team on the sub-block work.

decision.governing_rule: rule 2: lower level governs a split (autonomy/ownership indicate L1, problem complexity edges toward L2)
decision.alternative_reasoning: Problem complexity around CDC synchronization could be read as requiring judgment among known approaches (L2/L3 anchor), and carrying work through an actual tapeout is a real deliverable. However, autonomy ('under supervision') and scope (sub-block only, not a full block) are clearly L1, and per rule 2 the lower level governs absent unambiguous higher-level scope of impact.
decision.escalation_factor: problem_complexity -- whether the CDC synchronizer work reflects genuine judgment among known approaches (pushing toward L2) or fully directed execution (L1) would sharpen this call
decision.reasoning: Consistency check per section 6: source is a small company (headcount 104, late-stage private, whole-company, org_depth 4, low platform dependency). Per the expected-drift table, small-company titles map down 1-2 levels due to title inflation and shallow org depth. 'MTS I' (their entry-level title) mapping to Meridian L1 is consistent with this prior -- no title inflation contradiction observed, and low platform dependency means no cap adjustment needed on technical depth/breadth. This strengthens confidence in the L1 assignment.
